claim: Mammalian cells upregulate proteasome gene expression by activating Nrf1 in response to proteasome dysfunction.
source: In response to proteasome dysfunction, mammalian cells upregulate proteasome gene expression by activating Nrf1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known phenomenon in the field.

claim: Nrf1 is an endoplasmic reticulum-resident transcription factor.
source: Nrf1 is an endoplasmic reticulum-resident transcription factor that is continually retrotranslocated and degraded by the proteasome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about Nrf1.

claim: Nrf1 is continually retrotranslocated and degraded by the proteasome.
source: Nrf1 is an endoplasmic reticulum-resident transcription factor that is continually retrotranslocated and degraded by the proteasome.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about Nrf1 processing.

claim: Upon proteasome inhibition, Nrf1 escapes degradation and is cleaved to become active.
source: Upon proteasome inhibition, Nrf1 escapes degradation and is cleaved to become active.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about Nrf1 activation.

claim: The processing enzyme for Nrf1 remains obscure.
source: However, the processing enzyme for Nrf1 remains obscure.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The aspartyl protease DDI2 is required to cleave and activate Nrf1.
source: Here we show that the aspartyl protease DNA-damage inducible 1 homolog 2 (DDI2) is required to cleave and activate Nrf1.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Deletion of DDI2 reduced the cleaved form of Nrf1.
source: Deletion of DDI2 reduced the cleaved form of Nrf1 and increased the full-length cytosolic form of Nrf1, resulting in poor upregulation of proteasomes in response to proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Deletion of DDI2 increased the full-length cytosolic form of Nrf1.
source: Deletion of DDI2 reduced the cleaved form of Nrf1 and increased the full-length cytosolic form of Nrf1, resulting in poor upregulation of proteasomes in response to proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Deletion of DDI2 resulted in poor upregulation of proteasomes in response to proteasome inhibition.
source: Deletion of DDI2 reduced the cleaved form of Nrf1 and increased the full-length cytosolic form of Nrf1, resulting in poor upregulation of proteasomes in response to proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The defects caused by DDI2 deletion were restored by adding back wild-type DDI2.
source: These defects were restored by adding back wild-type DDI2 but not protease-defective DDI2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: The defects caused by DDI2 deletion were not restored by protease-defective DDI2.
source: These defects were restored by adding back wild-type DDI2 but not protease-defective DDI2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by rescue experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Nrf1 is the responsible transcription factor that upregulates expression of all proteasome subunit genes in a concerted manner in human cells.
source: Proteasome inhibition elicits a response to restore proteasome activity, or a 'bounce-back response,' where Nrf1 is the responsible transcription factor that upregulates expression of all proteasome subunit genes in a concerted manner in human cells (Radhakrishnan et al., 2010; Steffen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Proteasome inhibitors such as bortezomib and carfilzomib have been in clinical use for treatment of cancers, especially multiple myeloma.
source: Proteasome inhibitors such as bortezomib and carfilzomib have been in clinical use for treatment of cancers, especially multiple myeloma, but this bounce-back response attenuates the ability of proteasome inhibitors to kill cancer cells (Radhakrishnan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The bounce-back response attenuates the ability of proteasome inhibitors to kill cancer cells.
source: Proteasome inhibitors such as bortezomib and carfilzomib have been in clinical use for treatment of cancers, especially multiple myeloma, but this bounce-back response attenuates the ability of proteasome inhibitors to kill cancer cells (Radhakrishnan et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Genes regulating Nrf1 activation could be useful drug targets for increasing efficacy of proteasome inhibition in cancer treatment.
source: Therefore, genes regulating Nrf1 activation could be useful drug targets for increasing efficacy of proteasome inhibition in cancer treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical inference from the previous statement about the bounce-back response.

claim: When Nrf1 is produced, the bulk of the polypeptide is inserted into the ER lumen and glycosylated.
source: When Nrf1 is produced, the bulk of the polypeptide is inserted into the ER lumen and glycosylated, with a short cytosolic N-terminus followed by a single transmembrane domain (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Nrf1 has a short cytosolic N-terminus followed by a single transmembrane domain.
source: When Nrf1 is produced, the bulk of the polypeptide is inserted into the ER lumen and glycosylated, with a short cytosolic N-terminus followed by a single transmembrane domain (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The luminal region of Nrf1 is continually retrotranslocated to the cytosol by the p97/VCP ATPase complex.
source: The luminal region of Nrf1 is continually retrotranslocated to the cytosol by the p97/VCP ATPase complex, accompanied by deglycosylation and ubiquitination.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Nrf1 processing.

claim: Retrotranslocation of Nrf1 is accompanied by deglycosylation and ubiquitination.
source: The luminal region of Nrf1 is continually retrotranslocated to the cytosol by the p97/VCP ATPase complex, accompanied by deglycosylation and ubiquitination.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Nrf1 processing.

claim: Under normal circumstances, Nrf1 is promptly degraded by the proteasome.
source: Under normal circumstances, Nrf1 is promptly degraded by the proteasome.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about Nrf1 regulation.

claim: When proteasome activity is compromised, Nrf1 escapes degradation and is proteolytically cleaved to the active form which enters the nucleus.
source: In contrast, when proteasome activity is compromised, Nrf1 escapes degradation and is proteolytically cleaved to the active form which enters the nucleus and enhances expression of target genes including proteasome subunits (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014, 2010; Sha and Goldberg, 2014; Steffen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Active Nrf1 enhances expression of target genes including proteasome subunits.
source: In contrast, when proteasome activity is compromised, Nrf1 escapes degradation and is proteolytically cleaved to the active form which enters the nucleus and enhances expression of target genes including proteasome subunits (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014, 2010; Sha and Goldberg, 2014; Steffen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: A genome-wide siRNA screen was performed to identify genes important for Nrf1 activation.
source: To identify genes important for Nrf1 activation, we performed a genome-wide small interfering RNA (siRNA) screen (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental approach.

claim: The screening approach used the subcellular localization of Nrf1 accumulation in the nucleus in response to proteasome inhibition.
source: Our approach used the well-characterized subcellular localization of Nrf1 accumulation in the nucleus in response to proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the screening methodology.

claim: HEK293A cells were transfected with pooled siRNA and then treated with bortezomib to induce accumulation and nuclear translocation of Nrf1.
source: HEK293A cells were transfected with pooled siRNA (a pool of 4 unique siRNAs per gene) and then treated with the proteasome inhibitor bortezomib to induce accumulation and nuclear translocation of Nrf1 (Steffen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental procedure.

claim: p97 siRNA treatment abolished Nrf1 translocation following bortezomib treatment while increasing cytoplasmic Nrf1.
source: p97 siRNA treatment served as a positive control, which abolished Nrf1 translocation following bortezomib treatment while increasing cytoplasmic Nrf1 (Figure 1A) (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1A and a citation.

claim: The primary screen showed a high degree of assay robustness with Z'-factor > 0.5.
source: We observed a high degree of assay robustness (Z'-factor > 0.5, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C) in the primary screen.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The screen identified 14 candidate genes that may impair activation of Nrf1 in response to bortezomib treatment.
source: Consequently, we obtained 14 candidate genes that may impair activation of Nrf1 in response to bortezomib treatment (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1D.

claim: The screen hits included SEL1L, a co-factor of the ubiquitin ligase HRD1, which catalyzes ER-associated degradation (ERAD) of Nrf1.
source: These hits included SEL1L, a co-factor of the ubiquitin ligase HRD1, which catalyzes ER-associated degradation (ERAD) of Nrf1 (Iida et al., 2011; Steffen et al., 2010; Tsuchiya et al., 2011) and FAF2/UBXD8, a p97-recruiting molecule in ERAD (Meyer et al., 2012), validating our screening approach (Figure 1A,B, and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: The screen hits included FAF2/UBXD8, a p97-recruiting molecule in ERAD.
source: These hits included SEL1L, a co-factor of the ubiquitin ligase HRD1, which catalyzes ER-associated degradation (ERAD) of Nrf1 (Iida et al., 2011; Steffen et al., 2010; Tsuchiya et al., 2011) and FAF2/UBXD8, a p97-recruiting molecule in ERAD (Meyer et al., 2012), validating our screening approach (Figure 1A,B, and D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: DDI2 has a typical retroviral aspartyl protease domain.
source: Among the final hit genes, we focused on DDI2, because it has a typical retroviral aspartyl protease domain, and therefore is a candidate Nrf1 processing enzyme (Krylov and Koonin, 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: DDI2 knockdown partially inhibited nuclear translocation of Nrf1.
source: DDI2 knockdown partially inhibited nuclear translocation of Nrf1, accompanied by an increase in cytoplasmic Nrf1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: DDI2 knockdown was accompanied by an increase in cytoplasmic Nrf1.
source: DDI2 knockdown partially inhibited nuclear translocation of Nrf1, accompanied by an increase in cytoplasmic Nrf1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A.

claim: In negative control cells, Nrf1 was hardly detected in the absence of bortezomib.
source: In negative control cells, Nrf1 was hardly detected in the absence of bortezomib, but bortezomib treatment increased the processed, active form of Nrf1 as well as the full-length, cytosolic form that is retrotranslocated into the cytosol by p97 (Figure 2B) (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: Bortezomib treatment increased the processed, active form of Nrf1 in negative control cells.
source: In negative control cells, Nrf1 was hardly detected in the absence of bortezomib, but bortezomib treatment increased the processed, active form of Nrf1 as well as the full-length, cytosolic form that is retrotranslocated into the cytosol by p97 (Figure 2B) (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: Bortezomib treatment increased the full-length, cytosolic form of Nrf1 in negative control cells.
source: In negative control cells, Nrf1 was hardly detected in the absence of bortezomib, but bortezomib treatment increased the processed, active form of Nrf1 as well as the full-length, cytosolic form that is retrotranslocated into the cytosol by p97 (Figure 2B) (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: In p97 knockdown cells, the luminal ER form of Nrf1 that is N-glycosylated accumulated.
source: In p97 knockdown cells, the luminal ER form of Nrf1 that is N-glycosylated accumulated while the processed form almost disappeared both in the presence and absence of bortezomib.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: In p97 knockdown cells, the processed form of Nrf1 almost disappeared both in the presence and absence of bortezomib.
source: In p97 knockdown cells, the luminal ER form of Nrf1 that is N-glycosylated accumulated while the processed form almost disappeared both in the presence and absence of bortezomib.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: In DDI2 knockdown cells, Nrf1 was not detected in the absence of bortezomib.
source: In DDI2 knockdown cells, Nrf1 was not detected in the absence of bortezomib, similar to control cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: In DDI2 knockdown cells treated with bortezomib, the full-length, cytosolic form of Nrf1 markedly accumulated.
source: However, in the presence of bortezomib, the full-length, cytosolic form of Nrf1 markedly accumulated (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2B.

claim: DDI2 is involved in conversion of full-length, cytosolic Nrf1 to the processed, active form.
source: These results indicate that DDI2 is involved in conversion of full-length, cytosolic Nrf1 to the processed, active form.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: N-glycosylated Nrf1 accumulated in p97 knockdown cells was sensitive to endoglycosidase H (Endo H) treatment.
source: N-glycosylated Nrf1 accumulated in p97 knockdown cells was sensitive to endoglycosidase H (Endo H) treatment and the deglycosylated form migrated faster in SDS-PAGE, consistent with a previous report (Figure 2C) (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C and a citation.

claim: The deglycosylated form of Nrf1 migrated faster in SDS-PAGE.
source: N-glycosylated Nrf1 accumulated in p97 knockdown cells was sensitive to endoglycosidase H (Endo H) treatment and the deglycosylated form migrated faster in SDS-PAGE, consistent with a previous report (Figure 2C) (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C and a citation.

claim: The full-length form of Nrf1 accumulated in DDI2 knockdown cells was not sensitive to Endo H treatment.
source: In contrast, the full-length form of Nrf1 that is significantly accumulated in DDI2 knockdown cells was not sensitive to Endo H treatment (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C.

claim: The form of Nrf1 accumulated in DDI2-depleted cells is not N-glycosylated.
source: These results demonstrate that the form of Nrf1 accumulated in DDI2-depleted cells is not N-glycosylated, further supporting the role of DDI2 in the processing of Nrf1 rather than in deglycosylation or retrotranslocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the Endo H treatment data.

claim: DDI2 plays a role in the processing of Nrf1 rather than in deglycosylation or retrotranslocation.
source: These results demonstrate that the form of Nrf1 accumulated in DDI2-depleted cells is not N-glycosylated, further supporting the role of DDI2 in the processing of Nrf1 rather than in deglycosylation or retrotranslocation.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The X-ray crystal structure analysis of the retroviral aspartyl protease (RVP) domain of budding yeast Ddi1p revealed that it is a dimer with a similar fold to that of the HIV-1 protease.
source: The X-ray crystal structure analysis of the retroviral aspartyl protease (RVP) domain of budding yeast Ddi1p has revealed that it is a dimer with a similar fold to that of the human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) protease, with identical geometry of the double D[S/T]GA motif of the active site (Sirkis et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The RVP domain of yeast Ddi1p has identical geometry of the double D[S/T]GA motif of the active site to HIV-1 protease.
source: The X-ray crystal structure analysis of the retroviral aspartyl protease (RVP) domain of budding yeast Ddi1p has revealed that it is a dimer with a similar fold to that of the human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) protease, with identical geometry of the double D[S/T]GA motif of the active site (Sirkis et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The HIV-1 protease typically cleaves substrates between two hydrophobic residues.
source: The HIV-1 protease typically cleaves substrates between two hydrophobic residues (Konvalinka et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: Nrf1 is cleaved between Trp103 and Leu104 to become active.
source: Nrf1 has been shown to be cleaved between Trp103 and Leu104 to become active (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014), which conforms with the cleavage motif by retroviral aspartyl proteases.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation.

claim: The cleavage site of Nrf1 (between Trp103 and Leu104) conforms with the cleavage motif by retroviral aspartyl proteases.
source: Nrf1 has been shown to be cleaved between Trp103 and Leu104 to become active (Radhakrishnan et al., 2014), which conforms with the cleavage motif by retroviral aspartyl proteases.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference based on the known cleavage site and protease specificity.

claim: DDI2 has a ubiquitin-like domain (UBL) at the N-terminus.
source: DDI2 has a ubiquitin-like domain (UBL) at the N-terminus and a RVP domain near the C-terminus (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: DDI2 has a RVP domain near the C-terminus.
source: DDI2 has a ubiquitin-like domain (UBL) at the N-terminus and a RVP domain near the C-terminus (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Knockdown of DDI2 reduced the processed form of Nrf1 and increased full-length Nrf1.
source: Knockdown of DDI2 reduced the processed form and increased full-length Nrf1 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: The effect of DDI2 knockdown was rescued by introducing siRNA-resistant wild-type DDI2.
source: This effect was rescued by introducing siRNA-resistant wild-type DDI2 but not a protease-dead DDI2 in which the active site aspartic acid 252 was replaced with asparagine (D252N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: The effect of DDI2 knockdown was not rescued by protease-dead DDI2 (D252N).
source: This effect was rescued by introducing siRNA-resistant wild-type DDI2 but not a protease-dead DDI2 in which the active site aspartic acid 252 was replaced with asparagine (D252N).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: A DDI2 mutant lacking the UBL domain only partially restored the effect of DDI2 knockdown.
source: We also found that a DDI2 mutant lacking the UBL domain only partially restored the effect of DDI2 knockdown (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3B.

claim: The protease activity of DDI2 is required for cleavage of Nrf1.
source: These results suggest that the protease activity of DDI2 is required for cleavage of Nrf1 and that the UBL domain plays some role in the cleavage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the rescue experiments.

claim: The UBL domain of DDI2 plays some role in Nrf1 cleavage.
source: These results suggest that the protease activity of DDI2 is required for cleavage of Nrf1 and that the UBL domain plays some role in the cleavage.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the rescue experiments.

claim: In DDI2 knockout cells, the full-length form of Nrf1 was accumulated upon bortezomib treatment.
source: In DDI2 knockout cells and DDI2 D252N knock-in cells, the full-length form of Nrf1 was accumulated upon bortezomib treatment, whereas the processed form was accumulated in wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: In DDI2 D252N knock-in cells, the full-length form of Nrf1 was accumulated upon bortezomib treatment.
source: In DDI2 knockout cells and DDI2 D252N knock-in cells, the full-length form of Nrf1 was accumulated upon bortezomib treatment, whereas the processed form was accumulated in wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: In wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells, the processed form of Nrf1 was accumulated upon bortezomib treatment.
source: In DDI2 knockout cells and DDI2 D252N knock-in cells, the full-length form of Nrf1 was accumulated upon bortezomib treatment, whereas the processed form was accumulated in wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C.

claim: In parental HCT116 cells, bortezomib treatment caused an increase in mRNA levels of the proteasome subunit genes PSMA3 and PSMB5.
source: In parental HCT116 cells, bortezomib treatment caused an increase in mRNA levels of the proteasome subunit genes PSMA3 and PSMB5 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: Knockout of DDI2 strongly suppressed the upregulation of proteasome subunit genes in response to bortezomib.
source: Knockout of DDI2 strongly suppressed this response, further supporting the importance of DDI2 in Nrf1 activation (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: The basal expression of proteasome subunits was decreased in DDI2-deficient cells.
source: Interestingly, the basal expression of proteasome subunits was also decreased in DDI2-deficient cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: In wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells, mRNA levels of the proteasome subunits were upregulated in response to bortezomib, similar to the parental cells.
source: In wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells, mRNA levels of the proteasome subunits were upregulated in response to bortezomib, similar to the parental cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: DDI2 D252N knock-in cells did not undergo upregulation of proteasome subunit genes in response to bortezomib, similar to DDI2 knockout cells.
source: In contrast, DDI2 D252N knock-in cells did not undergo such a response, similar to DDI2 knockout cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: The processing of Nrf1 by the aspartyl protease activity of DDI2 is required for upregulation of proteasome gene expression mediated by Nrf1 in response to proteasome inhibition.
source: These results suggest that the processing of Nrf1 by the aspartyl protease activity of DDI2 is required for upregulation of proteasome gene expression mediated by Nrf1 in response to proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Nrf1 regulates basal expression of proteasome subunits, the extent of which varies between cell types.
source: Nrf1 has also been found to regulate basal expression of proteasome subunits, the extent of which varies between cell types (Lee et al., 2013, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with supporting citations.

claim: Knockout and D252N DDI2 knock-in cells had significantly lower proteasome activity compared to wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells.
source: We observed that knockout and D252N DDI2 knock-in cells had significantly lower proteasome activity compared to wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells, suggesting that DDI2 is also involved in basal expression of proteasomes through its catalytic activity (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3E.

claim: DDI2 is involved in basal expression of proteasomes through its catalytic activity.
source: We observed that knockout and D252N DDI2 knock-in cells had significantly lower proteasome activity compared to wild-type DDI2 knock-in cells, suggesting that DDI2 is also involved in basal expression of proteasomes through its catalytic activity (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the proteasome activity data.

claim: DDI2 is a protease that is required for Nrf1 processing and the bounce-back response induced by proteasome inhibition.
source: In conclusion, we identified DDI2 as a protease that is required for Nrf1 processing and the bounce-back response induced by proteasome inhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The cleavage site of Nrf1 (P1: W, P1': L) does not seem to be a sequence preferred by the proteasome.
source: In terms of substrate specificity, the cleavage site of Nrf1 (P1: W, P1': L) does not seem to be a sequence preferred by the proteasome (Toes et al., 2001); rather it conforms to a cleavage motif of RVP (Konvalinka et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The cleavage site of Nrf1 conforms to a cleavage motif of RVP.
source: In terms of substrate specificity, the cleavage site of Nrf1 (P1: W, P1': L) does not seem to be a sequence preferred by the proteasome (Toes et al., 2001); rather it conforms to a cleavage motif of RVP (Konvalinka et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: The proteasome activity may be required for function of DDI2 or some other factors involved in Nrf1 processing.
source: It could be that the proteasome activity is required for function of DDI2 or some other factors that is involved in Nrf1 processing.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation about the mechanism.

claim: DDI2 is not induced by bortezomib at either protein or mRNA level.
source: DDI2 is not induced by bortezomib at either protein or mRNA level (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The subcellular localization of DDI2 seems to be unaffected by bortezomib treatment.
source: Furthermore, the subcellular localization of DDI2 seems to be unaffected by bortezomib treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: DDI2 is suggested to be active even when the proteasome activity is not compromised.
source: Since DDI2 is suggested to be active even when the proteasome activity is not compromised (Figure 3D and E), a specific activation mechanism under proteasome impairment may not exist.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data in Figure 3D and E.

claim: A specific activation mechanism for DDI2 under proteasome impairment may not exist.
source: Since DDI2 is suggested to be active even when the proteasome activity is not compromised (Figure 3D and E), a specific activation mechanism under proteasome impairment may not exist.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation based on the data.

claim: The UBL domain of Ddi1p is an atypical UBL that binds ubiquitin.
source: It has been shown that the UBL domain of Ddi1p is an atypical UBL that binds ubiquitin (Nowicka et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: Binding of DDI2 with ubiquitinated proteins would be promoted by proteasome inhibition and may facilitate Nrf1 processing by DDI2.
source: Binding of DDI2 with ubiquitinated proteins, possibly Nrf1 itself, would be promoted by proteasome inhibition and may facilitate Nrf1 processing by DDI2.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Whether DDI2 directly cleaves Nrf1 remains unknown.
source: Lastly, whether DDI2 directly cleaves Nrf1 remains unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an open question.

claim: Recombinant DDI2 failed to cleave a recombinant fragment of Nrf1 encompassing the processing site in vitro.
source: We have tested a recombinant fragment of Nrf1 encompassing the processing site as a substrate for recombinant DDI2, but failed to detect its cleavage.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a negative result from an in vitro experiment.

claim: Other factors might be required for in vitro reconstitution of Nrf1 processing by DDI2.
source: Other factors might be required for in vitro reconstitution of Nrf1 processing by DDI2, such as substrate unfolding, co-activators of DDI2, and a set of specific experimental conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as speculation about why the in vitro experiment failed.

claim: Understanding the mechanism by which DDI2 cleaves Nrf1 should provide useful information for developing a DDI2 inhibitor.
source: Understanding the mechanism by which DDI2 cleaves Nrf1 and establishing an in vitro assay for the enzymatic activity of DDI2 should provide useful information for developing a DDI2 inhibitor that would block compensatory proteasome synthesis to improve cancer therapies targeting proteasomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential application of the research.

claim: A DDI2 inhibitor could block compensatory proteasome synthesis to improve cancer therapies targeting proteasomes.
source: Understanding the mechanism by which DDI2 cleaves Nrf1 and establishing an in vitro assay for the enzymatic activity of DDI2 should provide useful information for developing a DDI2 inhibitor that would block compensatory proteasome synthesis to improve cancer therapies targeting proteasomes.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a potential therapeutic application.

claim: The primary screen used a pool of 4 unique siRNAs per gene.
source: HEK293A cells were transfected with pooled siRNA (a pool of 4 unique siRNAs per gene) and then treated with the proteasome inhibitor bortezomib to induce accumulation and nuclear translocation of Nrf1 (Steffen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the screening methodology.

claim: The ratio of the nuclear to cytoplasmic fluorescent intensities was assessed by high-content microscopy and automated image analysis.
source: The ratio of the nuclear to cytoplasmic fluorescent intensities was assessed by high-content microscopy and automated image analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the screening methodology.

claim: Initial candidate genes with B score < –3.2 were selected for further testing.
source: The initial candidate genes with B score < –3.2 (Figure 1B) or which were picked up by visual inspection of the raw image data were further tested using four individual siRNAs in two different cell lines (HEK293A and HT1080 cells) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the screening workflow.

claim: Candidates with more than two hits in either cell line were examined for their effect on PSMA3 upregulation.
source: The subsequent candidates that had more than two hits in either cell line were finally examined whether the siRNAs mitigated upregulation of PSMA3, a proteasome subunit gene.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the screening workflow.

claim: Nrf1 is detected as three different forms: a glycosylated form (G), full-length form (FL), and processed form (P).
